title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations materially constrain inference and are explicitly disclosed: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) listed in the preregistration was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archived run. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR produced no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We release and analyze the authoritative archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) can increase NetOps throughput but raises safety concerns: stochastic generators sometimes output syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow ordering, or ACLs). Prior systems and surveys therefore recommend inserting deterministic validators and iterative repair loops (generate–verify–repair, GVR) between generation and execution to catch and correct mechanically checkable defects. Motivated by this operational question, we preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment that asked: Does a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (GVR) reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding alone on a public synthetic NetOps task bank? The preregistration (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) and all execution artifacts are archived and authoritative (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). Our contributions are (1) a fully preregistered paired evaluation using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic pybatfish-style validator on N=240 paired tasks, (2) transparent, artifact-backed execution accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240), (3) confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null outcome with explicit linkage to executed semantics and preregistered power assumptions, and (4) operationally grounded reproducibility recommendations and limitations.
sections.related_work: Three research strands frame this study. (1) LLM hallucination and code-generation failure analyses document frequent surface-level fabrication and incorrect tool/API usage in code- and configuration-generation tasks and motivate pipeline-level validators and repairs (survey and case-study literature). (2) Generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding techniques have demonstrable benefits for syntactic validity and executable artifacts in several domains, but prior work often measures surface-level or compilation properties rather than domain-specific semantic invariants used in NetOps. (3) NetOps-specific intent-translation and verifier literature emphasizes reachability- and policy-oriented validation and recommends human-in-the-loop controls for high-stakes changes. Our experiment differs by being preregistered, paired, and artifact-archived; it tests whether a bounded GVR loop yields measurable verifier-detectable gains under the executed design. The evidence-synthesis assembled for the run informed task-bank and oracle choices and identified open gaps: benchmark scope for semantic NetOps correctness and tighter LLM→formal-verifier integrations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation proportion, paired). Two primary comparisons were prespecified: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The preregistered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' was frozen before execution.

Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory sample N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks each). Requested generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing pybatfish-style checks and returning structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list). Crucial frozen semantics recorded prior to execution: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); maximum_model_calls = 480; execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. The preregistration and execution manifest were archived prior to observing outcomes.

Task bank and oracle: The public synthetic NetOps task bank encodes initial device states, intents, workflow constraints, and expected final states. The deterministic validator implements full_intent_constraint_validation; representative per-task validator traces (validation_before/after) are archived. Scoring: an output is scored as a verifier-acceptable configuration only when deterministic_netops_validator_v5 reports violation_count = 0 for the task’s encoded invariants.

Analysis plan: Primary analysis used the preregistered paired executor (exact McNemar two-sided test) with paired-bootstrap percentiles to compute 95% CIs (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and exclusion rules followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' policy. All scripts, seeds, and manifests were archived and are authoritative for every reported number.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics). Shared-generation semantics produced identical shared initial candidates per task that were reused across arms; repair loops never executed because the validator accepted the shared initial candidate for every task.

Primary outcomes: Contingency counts were n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Resulting summary: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. All analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair diagnostics: validator_trace entries in scored artifacts record repair_applied = false for every episode; the bounded repair loop was never invoked because no verifier-detected violations occurred. The contamination and missingness summaries show zero flags and zero failed episodes.

Statistical interpretation: Zero discordant pairs render the paired test degenerate: no within-pair information exists to estimate an effect under the executed shared-generation semantics, hence p = 1.00 and CI = [0.0,0.0] are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency and the preregistered analysis procedure. The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed shared-initial-candidate design; this preregistration→execution mismatch materially constrains inferential claims.
sections.discussion:
Conservative inference and mechanisms: Artifact-grounded evidence indicates two non-exclusive reasons for the null outcome. First, the generator+prompt pairing and the synthetic task-distribution aligned with the validator’s invariants so that the generator deterministically produced acceptable candidates. Second, the shared-generation evaluation semantics removed per-arm stochasticity and therefore eliminated the within-pair discordance that a GVR intervention could correct. Under these executed conditions bounded GVR could not demonstrate verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to repair.

Prespecified but unexecuted comparison: The preregistration explicitly listed two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed. No recorded operational rationale for this omission appears in the archive. We therefore label that prespecified comparison as unexecuted and unresolved in the present run — an explicit preregistration→execution deviation that limits interpretation regarding schema-constrained baselines.

Implications for evaluation practice: To measure whether GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under generator stochasticity, evaluations must restore within-pair variation (set independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks that reliably induce verifier failures, and/or expand generator diversity and repair budgets. The archived artifacts (task manifest, RNG seeds, adapter configuration) permit deterministic reruns that implement these alternatives.

Threats to validity: Internal validity: preregistration→execution mismatch (shared vs independent generation) compromises the preregistered power argument. Construct validity: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of operational risks outside the verifier’s encoded invariants. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic task bank, single bounded repair attempt, and single verifier implementation limit generalization. Conclusion validity: zero discordant pairs preclude evidence that bounded GVR improves verifier-detected outcomes under the executed semantics. These threats are documented in the archived limitations.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment (N = 240 paired tasks) to test whether a bounded GVR intervention reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→configuration NetOps. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate passed the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrapped 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Two preregistration→execution deviations substantially limit inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated preregistered independent-generation power assumptions, and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed (no recorded rationale in the archive). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We publish the authoritative artifacts to enable deterministic reruns under independent-generation semantics, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model comparisons, and expanded verifier coverage to more robustly evaluate GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore removed sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
